Source: A 3-day-old boy is evaluated in the neonatal intensive care unit for failure to pass meconium.
His abdomen is firm, non-tender, and distended with hypoactive bowel sounds.
He was born at 39 weeks gestation to a 38-year-old G3P3 mother.
The patient's temperature is 98.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure is 48/32 mmHg, pulse is 164/min, and respirations are 48/min.
The patient has had 2 episodes of vomiting that were described as green in color.
A digital rectal exam fails to relieve the obstruction.
The patient is otherwise doing well and feeding every 2 hours.
The pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the patient’s mother received routine prenatal care.
One of the patient’s older siblings has Down syndrome.
He is urinating 8-10 times per day.
An abdominal radiograph is performed and the result can be seen in Figure A.
On physical exam, the patient is in no acute distress.
